s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden collapse with ventricular fibrillation and subsequent coma
salient_findings: Coma with agonal respirations on examination
key_facts: 21-year-old woman with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability
On risperidone
No prior history of syncope, cardiac arrest, or known cardiovascular disease
Family denied any illicit drug or alcohol use
Collapse occurred at a noisy auto mechanic shop
Bystander ECG showed ventricular fibrillation
Return of spontaneous circulation achieved after two defibrillations
Blood pressure 93/70 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, and oxygen saturation 100% on arrival
Intravenous amiodarone infusion and oral amiodarone administered
Comatose with agonal respirations on examination
Cardiovascular examination was unremarkable
Normal chemistry panel and electrolytes
Sinus rhythm with interpolated premature ventricular complexes on electrocardiogram
QTc of 380 ms without evidence of infarction, pre-excitation, or Brugada pattern
Ejection fraction of 45-50% on transthoracic echocardiography
Normal wall thickness and no valvular abnormalities on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: QTc of 380 ms and ventricular fibrillation

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Family history and potential for sudden cardiac death

shortlist.label: Risperidone-induced QT prolongation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient on risperidone and QTc of 380 ms

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Ventricular fibrillation and potential for arrhythmia

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Ventricular fibrillation and potential for arrhythmia

raw.rationale: The patient's QTc interval of 380 ms is slightly prolonged, and she was taking risperidone, which is known to cause QT prolongation, increasing the risk of ventricular fibrillation and torsades de pointes.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: Although the QTc is slightly prolonged, it is not significantly prolonged enough to strongly suggest congenital Long QT syndrome, and the patient's age and presentation do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The echocardiogram showed normal wall thickness, which does not support a diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia or a family history to support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The echocardiogram did not show any evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or fibrofatty replacement, which is characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
